name: Multisystem Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis

criteria.description: Identification of Langerhans cells by immunohistochemistry positive for CD1a and/or Langerin (CD207)
Evidence of involvement of two or more organ systems (e.g., bone, skin, liver, lungs, hematopoietic system)
Characteristic radiologic findings such as lytic bone lesions or pulmonary cysts
Detection of BRAF V600E mutation in lesional tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of Langerhans cells plus multisystem clinical involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for BRAF mutations supports diagnosis and may guide therapy

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly affects skull, ribs, and long bones

laboratory: Anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukopenia in multisystem disease
Liver function abnormalities in hepatic involvement
imaging: Lytic bone lesions on X-ray or CT
Pulmonary cysts and nodules on chest CT
MRI showing pituitary stalk thickening or hypothalamic lesions
genetic: BRAF V600E mutation detected in lesional tissue in approximately 50-60% of cases
Other MAPK pathway mutations (e.g., MAP2K1) may be present
other: Immunohistochemistry positive for CD1a and Langerin (CD207)
Electron microscopy showing Birbeck granules in Langerhans cells

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of CD1a and Langerin positivity
Typically limited to skin and soft tissue without multisystem involvement
Systemic inflammatory response with cytopenias and organomegaly
Absence of Langerhans cells and characteristic histology
More common in adults, pulmonary and lymph node involvement

redFlags: Severe bone marrow suppression with pancytopenia
